papers.summary: In modular-arithmetic models, weight-rank compression follows grokking rather than causing it. A nuclear-norm penalty lowers effective rank but delays grokking in the tested MLP.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether training-induced compressibility tracks or improves generalization, using rank interventions and factorized controls.

evidence.quote: Compression is therefore a signature of grokking rather than its cause.

papers.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition

papers.summary: ProLand coordinates LoRA-factor updates in the represented weight-increment space and combines them with Muon-style spectral directions. It reports the highest mean score across seven decoder model–rank settings.
papers.relevance: Addresses the geometry and measured fine-tuning behavior of low-rank updates.

evidence.quote: ProLand forms a momentum input in the space of realizable first-order changes in B ​ A BA , computes its polar factor, and projects the result back into that space.
ProLand has the highest mean score in all seven reported model–rank settings (Tables 2 , 3 , and 4 ), with margins of 0.46 to 1.10 percentage points over the strongest baseline in each setting.

papers.title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning

papers.summary: Bi-Phase Training combines high-rank diagonal transformations with periodically merged low-rank adapters. At 1.5B parameters, it reports validation loss close to full training with 66% fewer trainable parameters and 5.8 GB lower peak GPU memory.
papers.relevance: A direct pretraining quality–memory tradeoff for low-rank parameterization across model sizes.

evidence.quote: We show that even with 66% less trainable parameters , BPT achieves validation loss close to full-parameter training.
Right: Peak GPU memory for Qwen-2.5-1.5B. BPT saves 5.8 GB to train a 1.5B model.

papers.title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch

papers.summary: TUON uses tensor-SVD-based cross-layer mixing and polarization. It reports lower validation loss than Muon and TEON at four tested pretraining scales, while its iteration time exceeds AdamW's by 3.5%–12.5%.
papers.relevance: Tests spectral matrix-optimization ideas against quality and training-speed baselines at LLM scale.

evidence.quote: TUON achieves the lowest loss on three of the four settings and consistently outperforms Muon and TEON.
Relative to vector-aware AdamW, TUON is slower by 6.1 % 6.1\\% , 8.3 % 8.3\\% , 3.5 % 3.5\\% , and 12.5 % 12.5\\% on the four models per iteration, respectively.

papers.title: TUON: A Tensor-Aware Optimizer Utilizing Tensor-SVD and Polarization for Large Language Model Pretraining

papers.summary: Dobb computes matrix-aware updates within parameter shards. On GPT-2 XL, it reports validation loss of 2.476 versus Dion's 2.511 at the compared configuration, and an amortized optimizer-call time of 9.2 versus 124.1 ms under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses optimizer communication, quality, and speed in sharded language-model training.

evidence.quote: Dobb reaches a validation loss of 2.476 against 2.511 for Dion (Table 4 ), and under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs, its amortized optimizer call takes 9.2 ms against 124.1 ms
The count excludes forward-backward communication and Dobb’s separately counted data-parallel synchronization of activation second moments (Section 5 ).

papers.title: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases

papers.summary: This scientific-paper retrieval study measures how shared names hinder identification and compares title BM25, title-plus-abstract E5, and listwise ranking under explicit candidate-set conditions.
papers.relevance: Directly informs paper discovery and relevance ranking in a research-digest agent.

evidence.quote: Shared-name targets remain 25.7 points behind matched unique-name targets under title-based BM25 and 6.9 points behind under title-plus-abstract E5.
Within complete same-name candidate sets, contextual ranking reaches 70.6% with BM25, 89.2% with a language model, and 93.6% with E5 over titles and abstracts.

papers.title: "PRISM" Is Not All You Need: Cross-Topic Name Collisions and Scientific Paper Retrieval

papers.summary: A structured decision model can rerank competitively after input-length controls, but the tuned dedicated reranker remains faster and uses less GPU memory. The paper evaluates reliability and fallbacks alongside ranking quality.
papers.relevance: Provides practical controls for deciding whether structured LLM decisions belong in the digest's retrieval harness.

evidence.quote: The default decision-model setup fails on many long candidate sets, so scoring only the requests it completes gives a misleading ranking.
Across workloads, which model ranks better changes, and a tuned reranker remains faster and uses far less GPU memory.

papers.title: Can System-1-Style Decision Models Replace Dedicated Rerankers in RAG? A Systems Evaluation
